items.title: Build a Local Router with Nemotron Lightning
items.summary:
Thanks to ‪@NVIDIADeveloper‬ for DGX Spark. Check it out here:  https://nvda.ws/3XIkwsh 

In this video I explain why a routing layer is becoming essential for agentic systems and show how to run your own router locally so you control cost, speed, specialization, and privacy. I compare proprietary and open-source options (OpenRouter, Devin Fusion, RouteLLM) and then focus on NVIDIA Switchyard (built on RouteLLM) and how it supports multiple routing strategies: random, LLM classifier, stage routing, and escalation—plus their cost tradeoffs. I also cover NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (30B latent MoE) and why its high throughput matters, including a speed test versus Kimi K3. Finally, I demo local-first alert analysis workflows where Nemotron generates private digests and Switchyard escalates to Kimi K3 only when needed, and explain why routing should be done per task/session rather than per turn.

items.title: Full Platform Overview | H2O.ai Managed Cloud
items.summary:
H2O.ai Managed Cloud is a fully managed, isolated AI environment where data preparation, model development, and deployment all run in one place.

This first lesson covers what the platform is and the problem it solves. Most teams are not short of ideas, they are slowed down by data living in one system, models being built in another, and deployment happening somewhere else.

You will also see the two principles behind the setup. Managed means H2O.ai runs the infrastructure for you, including GPU compute when the workload needs it. Isolated means your environment is dedicated, so data, compute, and workloads are never shared with another customer.

Covered in this video:
The three capabilities the platform brings together: automated machine learning, generative AI, and model operations
Why fragmented tooling causes delays, duplicated effort, and gaps in governance
Where H2O Driverless AI, H2O LLM Studio, and Enterprise h2oGPTe sit in the platform
What managed and isolated mean for security, privacy, and enterprise governance

items.title: The RAG Mistake Almost Every Team Is Making (with Pete Johnson)
items.summary:
#VectorSearch #AgenticMemory #RAG

In Episode #1017, Pete Johnson (Field CTO of AI at MongoDB) joins Jon Krohn to explain why four out of five organizations have AI steering committees and success metrics, yet only one in five sees a return on the investment. Having made nineteen stops across six countries this year advising more than a hundred companies on their AI strategies, Pete has an unusually wide view of what is actually working in production. In this episode, he traces the history of SQL and denormalization, unpacks why the embedding model is the most underrated choice in a RAG pipeline, explains Matryoshka embeddings and lays out what better agentic memory looks like.

items.title: Building Specialized AI Systems
items.summary:
Walid Amamou and Alessandro Negro teach you how to adapt pre-trained language models to your exact domain, data, and operational constraints in their latest book, Building Specialized AI Systems.

In this session, we’ll ask these questions:

1. When is a general purpose LLM not enough for a real business problem?
2. How do you know when to fine-tune instead of just prompting better?
3. What problems do specialized AI systems solve that off-the-shelf models can’t?
4. Why do so many fine-tuning projects fail before they reach production?
5. What kind of data do teams actually need to build a useful specialized model?
6. How can smaller, specialized models compete with larger frontier models?
7. How should teams choose between fine-tuning, RAG, agents, or a hybrid approach?
8. What are the biggest mistakes developers make when building AI agents?
9. How do you evaluate whether a specialized AI system is truly improving?
10. How can teams control cost, latency, and reliability when moving from prototype to production?

This is a live, interactive session, feel free to add your questions in the comments.
 
We will also giveaway Ebooks to 2 lucky winners during the session. Comment #AI to enter the raffle!

items.title: Introducing ExtractBench: The Most Comprehensive Benchmark for Data Extraction from Enterprise Docs
items.summary:
LlamaIndex is open sourcing the first schema-guided document extraction benchmark for the agentic era, ExtractBench. Document extraction is the foundation of every AI agent that operates on real-world enterprise files. But as agents gain autonomy and humans step out of the loop, existing benchmarks fall short of measuring extraction quality across the requirements production actually demands.

ExtractBench is an open-source benchmark testing 370 enterprise documents (4,869 pages) across 67 document schemas and 8 business domains. It jointly evaluates systems across the four dimensions production cares about most: long-record completeness, spatial visual grounding, perception robustness, and per-page cost.

LlamaExtract Agentic Plus was the only system to score above 90 on every dimension, leading the board at 95.6% overall.

Blogpost:https://www.llamaindex.ai/blog/introducing-extractbench

But as agents gain autonomy and humans step out of the loop, existing benchmarks fall short of measuring extraction quality across the requirements production actually demands.

ExtractBench is an open-source benchmark testing 370 enterprise documents (4,869 pages) across 67 document schemas and 8 business domains. It jointly evaluates systems across the four dimensions production cares about most: long-record completeness, spatial visual grounding, perception robustness, and per-page cost.

LlamaExtract Agentic Plus was the only system to score above 90 on every dimension, leading the board at 95.6% overall.

items.title: Deep Dive into Long-List Completeness: Evaluating Extraction Completeness on Long Documents
items.summary:
ExtractBench is an open benchmark for schema-guided document extraction. This deep dive looks at long-list completeness: how extraction systems handle multi-page, record-heavy enterprise files.

Every commercial VLM we tested scores well on short documents, then falls below 35% recall on documents past 50 pages, while precision stays high. The values that come back are correct. Most of the list doesn't come back at all.

ExtractBench scores long-list completeness with deterministic Hungarian alignment for record arrays and no LLM judge, so recall is measured exactly across complex schemas and multi-page filings, not estimated.

Read more about ExtractBench here: https://www.llamaindex.ai/blog/introducing-extractbench

items.title: Deep Dive into Perception: Scoring Scans, Handwriting, and Rotated Pages
items.summary:
ExtractBench is an open benchmark for schema-guided document extraction. This deep dive looks at perception: how extraction systems handle documents that don't arrive as clean, born-digital text.

ExtractBench tags every document by how the page was captured: born-digital, scanned, handwritten, or rotated. A system that reasons perfectly can still misread a smudged 5 as an 8.

The two frontier coding agents we tested have a perception blind spot, in opposite directions. One reads scans and handwriting well but stumbles on rotated pages. The other handles rotation and falls apart on scans and handwriting. LlamaExtract Agentic Plus is the only system that stays above 93% on all three.

Read more about ExtractBench here: https://www.llamaindex.ai/blog/introducing-extractbench

items.title: Deep Dive into Visual Grounding: Measuring Bounding Boxes and Citation Accuracy in Document AI
items.summary:
ExtractBench is an open benchmark for schema-guided document extraction. In this video, we do a deep dive into visual grounding and measuring word- and page-level spatial citations.

When AI agents execute autonomous workflows, auditability is critical. An extraction system cannot just return a text value; it must prove exactly where on the physical page that value originated.

We score spatial grounding deterministically using word- and page-level bounding box overlap. This tests whether models can emit verifiable visual citations back to the source document for enterprise compliance and human auditability.

Read more about ExtractBench here:https://www.llamaindex.ai/blog/introducing-extractbench
